L'homme de bien n'attend point la perfection d'une personne ordinaire. [§§§§§§責備於一人"demand the provision of everything from one single person" is misconstrued in the English, which gets nowhere with 責備. 許匡一：所以君子对一个人不要求十全十美。 is much better than 陳廣忠：因此君子对任何一个人都不应求全责备。"does not demand perfection from anyone" does not adequately account for the meaning of 一人. Pomeranceva has no problem with this one: Вот почему благородный муж не требует совершенства от одного человека, "the gentleman does not demand perfection from one person".

Dans l'Antiquité, ceux qui régnaient sur le monde portaient un simple bonnet et un col de fourrure roulé. [§§§§§§古者 “In prehistoric times (before the 三皇 Three Sovereigns)“ is the correct gloss of the old commentary which is overlooked by most translators. Liu Kangde's "遠古 gets the message. The English "in ancient times" is deeply misleading. §§§§§有"there were those who" is misinterpreted in the English. "In ancient times there were those who wore... and (yet) ruled the world) is the Chinese construction." Not ALL rulers necessarily wore this uncivilised military headgear, according to 陳廣忠: 有头戴兜婺翻卷领部而统冶天下的 gets the grammar right, and so does 劉康德. ]

Leur vertu se manifestait par la vie et non par la mort, [§§§§§德"natural (charismatic) feature/practice" is misunderstood by the mechanically "correct" English translation "Potency" (which in itself - by the way - is very often very helpful, sed non nunc, et non hic, but not here and not now). Even 陳廣忠 can only offer a paraphrase, but his is a helpful one, and much clearer than the English: 他们实行德政使人民繁衍而不加杀害. I suggest: "as for their moral charisma it promoted life and did not take life (through punishments etc)" 高注：刑措不用也。Pomeranceva: Их благой силы (дэ) было достаточно, чтобы рождать, а не позорить,] ”Their virtue was designed to give/promote life, not to administer death."

le yin et le yang étaient dans un équilibre harmonieux, [§和平 is one binome, not two words. 陰陽"the (potential conflicting) cosmic energies of Yin and Yang" are what is really referred to here, not the concepts of Yin and Yang themselves, I think. 許匡一 has the subtle point precisely: 在那时候，阴气、阳气平平和和.]

On pouvait, en abaissant les nids prendre les corbeaus et les pies dans ses mains. [§§§§§§烏 “crow” is not 鳥，and §§§§§§鵲 is "magpie" and a magpie is not an owl. I think the point is that the birds built their nests so low never having to fear that humans would cruelly reach down into their nests to take the eggs. §§§俯 "bending down" does not involve bending one's knees as the English has it, and there is no question of "lowering the nests, as the French would have it. §§探 "catch sight of, explore" is probably not best taken in the meaning "take, grasp" here, as Robinet has noticed.]

Dans l'Antiquité, le peuple habitait les marais, et les grottes a flanc des montagnes. [§§§§復穴"earth caves"HYDCD16.地室。《詩·大雅·綿》：“古公亶父，陶復陶穴，未有家室。”《商君書·徠民》：“人之復陰陽澤水者過半。”一說爲開掘於住穴之內的竇窖。參閱於省吾《澤螺居詩經新證·陶復陶穴》。There is no "again and again" here. The important literary allusion missed by the English is to the Odes.]

Alors apparut un saint qui lui fit des habitations en damant la terre et en dressant des charpentes de bois. [聖人”sagely creative individuals (not any grand named mythological cultural giants of the 神農 type)" does not here refer to any particular sage, or to any particular identifiable set of sages. The question how exactly this occurrence of "聖人“ has to be taken is not addressed in the Chinese translations. I suggest that the reference is indefinite as in "Sages>Sagely individuals", people of radically superior original and creatuve wisdom.] [§§§§§構木 "fit timber together (for the construction of buildings)" is not well rendered by "the cutting of trees". §§§§§作"arise" is not recognised in the English, and also not by DS. 高注”作， 起也”. Note that here the crucial role of the sages is indeed focussed here, and the question is how general the scope is of this focus. See Comments on this line待考]
